name: Miss Fortune
notes: The engine casts Bullet Time (R) at t=0 per its opening hook; its 0.001s cast time is spent first (busy_for), then the up-to-3s channel itself holds every other action, so Love Tap's one-time bonus lands on whichever basic attack or Double Up follows the channel.

Double Up's cast time is read literally as 'Basic Attack Timer': it can only be cast when the attack timer is ready, and casting it consumes that attack's slot (the next auto-attack is pushed back by a full attack period instead of the usual 0.25s cast lockout).
Double Up counts as an on-attack effect, so it can proc Love Tap the same as a basic attack, per the ability's own text ('applying on-attack effects to the primary target').

Double Up's primary hit crits at the engine's normal expected rate; the reduced 50%-bonus crit multiplier and the bounce hit never occur, since a 1v1 dummy fight has no secondary target behind the primary.
Love Tap can only proc once against a single dummy (its mark never expires without a second enemy to attack); its bonus damage does not crit.
Landing Love Tap's mark cuts Strut's current cooldown by a flat 2s, per the wiki's stated value; the bin's ability-haste-scaling multiplier on that refund is unresolved, so it is treated as flat.

Bullet Time's cast time (0.001s, the sheet's own number) is spent as a real cast before the channel starts; its waves are timed from the cast at 0.05s to 2.9s, evenly spread across the wave count, and every other action (attacks, Double Up, Strut, Make It Rain) is held for the whole channel and resumes once the last wave fires, per the wiki's note that the final ~0.1s can be cancelled at no loss.
Each Bullet Time wave crits independently at a reduced 30%-bonus multiplier; its expected value is folded into the wave's damage rather than using the engine's standard (full) crit handling.
Strut (W) is cast purely for its attack-speed active on cooldown; its passive movement-speed bonus does not affect damage and is ignored.
Make It Rain's cooldown is set at the moment of cast (not when its dots finish), since the wiki gives no post-effect timing for it.
Mana costs are not modeled: Miss Fortune's level-16 mana pool comfortably covers this rotation within a 15s fight.
